title: Hugging Face CEO said that open-weight AI models are helping China win
excerpt: Clément Delangue said the Hugging Face hack showed that open-weight models are vital for AI defense.
content_html:
Hugging Face CEO says China is winning the AI race while the US is building 'in silos'

By Katherine Li

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

The Hugging Face CEO is making a case for open-weight AI models — with a warning for the US.

Clément Delangue said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" show on Monday that China is winning the AI race because the country is "more open science and open models than the US."

"I think they are," Delangue said Monday on CNBC when asked by host Sara Eisen whether China is winning the AI race. "So there's this kind of emulation and the rate of progress is much faster there than in the US, where everyone is building in silos in some of the frontier labs and not sharing with the rest of the ecosystem."

He added, "I wouldn't be surprised if they start dominating at the frontier in general, not just open models, either by the end of this year or next year at the rate of progress."

The debate over open-weight AI has intensified after a July incident in which an OpenAI agent escaped a training environment and hacked Hugging Face's platform. Delangue previously said he had turned to GLM 5.2, an open-source model from Beijing-based Z.ai, to help defend the company's system.

"We were attacked by an unreleased private model built behind closed door," he said. "And we could only defend ourselves with open models because the guardrails of the APIs didn't let us."

"I think in the future we'll see that most of the attacks are actually going to come from private proprietary models because the attackers, they don't care about guardrails," he added. "They don't care about terms of service, and most of the defense will actually be done by open models."

The remarks land as policymakers debate whether open-weight AI from China should face tighter restrictions.

In late July, over two dozen tech companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, and OpenAI, signed a letter urging US policymakers not to crack down on open-weight AI models. Days later, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei clarified his company's stance on the issue in a blog post. "Open-weights models that don't have dangerous capabilities are a public good," he wrote.

Hugging Face首席执行官表示，中国正在赢得人工智能竞赛，而美国正在“孤岛”建设

作者：Katherine Li 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

Hugging Face 首席执行官正在为开放权重人工智能模型辩护——并对美国发出警告。

克莱门特·德朗格 (Clément Delangue) 周一在 CNBC 的“Squawk on the Street”节目中表示，中国正在赢得人工智能竞赛，因为该国“比美国更加开放的科学和开放的模式”。

“我认为是的，”德兰格周一在 CNBC 节目中被主持人萨拉·艾森问及中国是否正在赢得人工智能竞赛时说道。 “因此，存在这种模拟，而且进展速度比美国快得多，在美国，每个人都在一些前沿实验室的孤岛中进行建设，而不与生态系统的其他部分共享。”

他补充道，“如果他们开始在整个前沿领域占据主导地位，而不仅仅是开放模型，无论是在今年年底还是明年，以进展速度，我都不会感到惊讶。”

7 月份发生的一起 OpenAI 代理逃离训练环境并入侵 Hugging Face 平台的事件之后，有关开放权重 AI 的争论愈演愈烈。 Delangue 此前表示，他已转向 GLM 5.2（北京再爱科技的开源模型）来帮助保护该公司的系统。

“我们受到了一个秘密建造的未发布的私人模型的攻击，”他说。 “我们只能通过开放模型来保护自己，因为 API 的护栏不允许我们这样做。”

“我认为将来我们会看到大多数攻击实际上来自私人专有模型，因为攻击者不关心护栏，”他补充道。 “他们不关心服务条款，大部分防御实际上将通过开放模型完成。”

这一言论发表之际，政策制定者正在争论来自中国的开放式人工智能是否应该面临更严格的限制。

7 月下旬，包括英伟达、微软、Meta 和 OpenAI 在内的二十多家科技公司签署了一封信，敦促美国政策制定者不要打击开放权重人工智能模型。 几天后，Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 在一篇博文中澄清了公司在这个问题上的立场。 “不具有危险功能的开放权重模型是一种公共物品，”他写道。
